subject: mining-engineering
intro: Mining engineering leads to the engineers and technicians who find, extract and process the minerals modern life runs on — and who make that extraction safe, economic and environmentally survivable.

roles.title: Mining and Geological Engineers, Including Mining Safety Engineers
roles.what: Conduct subsurface surveys of potential mining sites, specify ground support systems, processes and equipment for safe, economical and environmentally sound extraction, inspect for unsafe geological conditions, and coordinate mine safety programs.
roles.where: This is the syllabus in job form — ore deposit geology and reserve estimation, open-pit and underground method design, ground control and ventilation, and the safety systems and mine valuation topics of the final unit.

roles.title: Petroleum Engineers
roles.what: Devise methods to improve oil and gas extraction and production, decide when new or modified tool designs are needed, and oversee drilling operations while advising on technique.
roles.where: Drilling and fragmentation, haulage and equipment, and reserve estimation from the course transfer to hydrocarbon extraction, with the mine valuation economics unit covering the production decisions engineers make.

roles.title: Geological Technicians, Except Hydrologic Technicians
roles.what: Assist scientists and engineers with measuring instruments in exploration and production, obtaining data on resources such as metallic ore, minerals, gas, coal or petroleum, and analysing mud and drill cuttings.
roles.where: The exploration methods and ore deposit geology units, plus reserve estimation, are exactly the field and laboratory work geological technicians carry out on a mining project.

roles.title: Environmental Engineers
roles.what: Research, design and plan engineering responses to environmental hazards: waste treatment, site remediation and pollution control technology, frequently applied around mining and heavy industry.
roles.where: The tailings management and environmental stewardship topics, mine closure planning, and water-penetration thinking from the safety, environment and economics unit are the daily substance of mining-side environmental engineering.

roles.title: Engineering Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach university courses applying physical laws and engineering principles to machines, materials, processes and services — including mineral engineering — usually combining teaching with research.
roles.where: Every unit of this programme is material a mineral-engineering lecturer teaches: surface and underground methods, mineral processing, ground control, and mine economics — the last usually from an active research programme.
